subject: physics
introduction: Quick-reference formulas and units for CSEC Physics Paper 1 and Paper 2. All SI units are given — always show the formula, substitution, and unit in calculations.

items.name: Average speed
items.notes: Distance in metres, time in seconds. Convert km/h to m/s by dividing by 3.6.

items.name: Acceleration
items.notes: u = initial velocity, v = final velocity. Deceleration gives a negative value.

items.name: Newton's second law
items.notes: Weight is a force: W = m × g, with g = 10 N/kg (or 10 m/s²) on Earth.

items.name: Momentum
items.notes: Conserved in collisions: total momentum before = total momentum after.

items.name: Kinetic energy
items.notes: Doubling speed quadruples kinetic energy.

items.name: Gravitational potential energy
items.notes: Energy gained lifting a mass h metres against gravity.

items.name: Work done
items.notes: Force must act in the direction of motion; 1 J = 1 N·m.

items.name: Power
items.formula: P = W / t = E / t  (W = J/s)
items.notes: 1 kW = 1000 W. Electrical power: P = V × I = I²R = V²/R.

items.name: Efficiency
items.notes: Always less than 100% — the rest is wasted, usually as heat.

items.name: Pressure (solids/fluids)
items.notes: Hydraulics: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂. Liquid pressure: P = ρ × g × h.

items.name: Archimedes / floating
items.notes: An object floats when its weight equals the upthrust; density of object < density of fluid.

items.name: Kelvin conversion
items.notes: Gas-law calculations MUST use kelvin. 0 °C = 273 K.

items.name: Boyle's law (constant T)
items.notes: Pressure × volume is constant; halving volume doubles pressure.

items.name: Charles' law (constant P)
items.notes: Volume proportional to absolute temperature.

items.name: Pressure law (constant V)
items.notes: Pressure proportional to absolute temperature.

items.name: General gas law
items.notes: Combined form — the workhorse for CSEC gas calculations.

items.name: Heat energy
items.notes: c = specific heat capacity (water: 4200 J/kg°C).

items.name: Latent heat
items.notes: l = specific latent heat; temperature stays constant during melting/boiling.

items.name: Linear expansion
items.notes: α = linear expansivity. Explains expansion gaps in rails and bridges.

items.name: Wave equation
items.notes: f = frequency (Hz), λ = wavelength (m). Period T = 1/f.

items.name: Speed of sound in air
items.notes: Sound needs a medium — it cannot travel through a vacuum.

items.name: Speed of light
items.notes: Fastest possible speed; EM waves all travel at this speed in vacuum.

items.name: Law of reflection
items.formula: angle of incidence = angle of reflection
items.notes: Both angles measured from the normal, not the surface.

items.name: Refractive index
items.formula: n = sin i / sin r = speed in vacuum / speed in medium
items.notes: Bending toward the normal when entering a denser medium.

items.name: Critical angle & TIR
items.notes: Total internal reflection when incidence exceeds c; used in optical fibres.

items.name: Lens power (qualitative)
items.formula: converging (convex) lens focuses parallel rays to focal point
items.notes: Real images form where rays meet and can be caught on a screen.

items.name: Charge flow
items.notes: Current is the rate of flow of charge.

items.name: Potential difference
items.notes: Energy transferred per unit charge across a component.

items.name: Ohm's law
items.notes: Only for ohmic conductors at constant temperature.

items.name: Resistors in series
items.notes: Same current everywhere; voltages add.

items.name: Resistors in parallel
items.notes: Same voltage across each branch; currents add.

items.name: Electrical energy
items.formula: E = V × I × t = P × t  (J; 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ)
items.notes: Domestic bills use kilowatt-hours: E(kWh) = power(kW) × time(h).

items.name: Transformer turns ratio
items.notes: Step-up: more secondary turns (higher V, lower I). Works on AC only, via electromagnetic induction.

items.name: Half-life
items.notes: After n half-lives: A = A₀ / 2ⁿ. Alpha = helium nucleus, beta = fast electron, gamma = EM wave (most penetrating).
